headline: Managing Campsite and Activity Access on the Saint John River
reservation: Entry for day use generally follows a standard gate fee system, but the expansive campground requires advance booking via the Parks New Brunswick site. Demand is high for riverside spots; verify the current seasonal opening dates and reservation launch schedule officially to secure specific amenities.

days.title: River Valley Recreation

stops.name: Mactaquac Beaver Pond Trail
stops.detail: Walk the accessible boardwalk to observe local wetland ecosystems and active beaver lodges in a serene setting.

stops.name: Mactaquac Dam
stops.detail: View the impressive hydroelectric infrastructure from designated public areas to understand the river's modern significance.

days.driving: Allow 20-30 minutes from Fredericton; roads are well-maintained.
days.note: The dam viewpoint is best accessed during daylight for safety.

days.title: High Canopy and Waterways

stops.name: TreeGO Mactaquac
stops.detail: Navigate the aerial obstacle course for a unique perspective of the New Brunswick forest canopy.

stops.name: Main Beach Area
stops.detail: Enjoy the freshwater swimming and sandy shores of the 'headpond' created by the river's redirection.

days.driving: Local transit within the park is minimal; facilities are clustered.
days.note: Water activities are subject to seasonal lifeguard availability.

days.title: Golf and Greenways

stops.name: Mactaquac Golf Course
stops.detail: Play a round at one of the province's premier public courses, noted for its mature trees and river valley views.

stops.name: Alex Creek Trail
stops.detail: A quieter hiking option that winds through diverse woodland and offers a break from the busier recreational hubs.

days.driving: Travel between the golf course and trails is under 10 minutes.
days.note: Golf tee times should be coordinated through the park’s specialized booking system.

intel.title: Beach and Trail Lots
intel.text: Primary parking is available at the lodge and beach; peak summer weekends may see lots reaching capacity by midday.

intel.title: Standard Service
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong due to the proximity to Fredericton and local utility infrastructure.

intel.title: Regional Stations
intel.text: Fuel is readily available in Fredericton and smaller stations along Highway 105; check hours for rural kiosks.

intel.title: Summer Programming
intel.text: Interpretive programs and water activities are most frequent between late June and Labor Day.

intel.title: Accessibility Features
intel.text: The Beaver Pond Trail offers a specialized boardwalk for users with mobility considerations; check for recent maintenance updates.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at YFC and drive west on Route 102 or 105; stock up on essentials in Fredericton before arriving at the park gate.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are perfect; the park roads are fully paved and facilitate easy RV maneuvering.
plan.goldenHour: The Mactaquac Headpond shoreline for sunset views across the widened Saint John River.
